property_summary: Any non-admin caller can successfully execute newEmergencyOracle
A caller that is not an admin cannot successfully execute newEmergencyOracle.
A non-admin caller can successfully create a new EmergencyOracle via newEmergencyOracle, which should revert in the original but always succeeds in the mutant.
A caller who is not an admin cannot successfully invoke newEmergencyOracle.

For any admissible description and admin, the newly created EmergencyOracle's owner must be msg.sender (the admin), but the mutant uses address(this) as owner, so calling owner() on the new contract returns C's address instead of the admin's address.

For any admin caller, after calling newEmergencyOracle with any description, the emitted event's owner field (from the NewEmergencyOracle event) equals the caller, but the buggy version uses a different owner address (address(this)).
For any admin caller and any description, the owner of the newly deployed EmergencyOracle contract must be the admin (msg.sender); the buggy version makes it address(this).

For any admin and description, calling newEmergencyOracle creates an EmergencyOracle whose owner is the caller (msg.sender); the buggy version sets the owner to C's address, so the owner() of the created contract differs.
After any admin calls newEmergencyOracle, the returned oracle token's owner() equals msg.sender, but the buggy version returns address(this) instead.
The EmergencyOracle created by newEmergencyOracle should be owned by msg.sender. The bug passes address(0) as the owner, so the resulting oracle's owner() returns address(0), violating the invariant.

The newEmergencyOracle function should always create a new EmergencyOracle whose owner() matches the msg.sender at the time of the call; the bug passes address(0) as owner, so a subsequent attempt by the original caller to call an onlyOwner function on the created oracle (like setAssetPrice) reverts due to Ownable._checkOwner failing.

For any admin caller and any description, after newEmergencyOracle(description) returns, there exists an EmergencyOracle contract whose owner is the caller; the bug creates an oracle owned by address(0), making it impossible for the original caller to later turn on the oracle.

After any admin calls newEmergencyOracle, calling getAssetPrice() on the returned EmergencyOracle always reverts because no one can turn it on; the bug makes it revert unconditionally for a different reason (turnOn is false) but the correct version additionally fails because the admin can later set a price on an oracle they own, making the behavior distinguishable once the oracle is activated by its owner.
